svg.title: The Harlot and the Bride
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 8 panels. Two columns side by side: The harlot and The Bride, row for row. Panel 1 (Revelation 17:1): John standing on a plain at dusk, looking up toward a voice from above. Caption: "One of the seven angels to John." The angel says: "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute". Panel 2 (Revelation 21:9): John standing at dawn, looking up toward a voice from above. Caption: "The same angel’s words, again." The angel says: "Come, I will show you the Bride, the wife of the Lamb." A strip joins the panels above: Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι, “Come, I will show you”: the same words for both women. Panel 3 (Revelation 17:3-4): the harlot seated, in purple and a scarlet veil with a gold girdle, holding up a golden cup. Caption: "In a wilderness: purple, scarlet and gold." John says: "holding in her hand a golden cup full of abominations". Panel 4 (Revelation 19:7-8): the Bride standing in bright white linen, arms raised. Caption: "The Bride, made ready." John says: "it was granted her to clothe herself with fine linen, bright and pure". Panel 5 (Revelation 18:23): an empty street at night, a wall cracking and falling, no one in it. Caption: "Her end: silence." John says: "the voice of bridegroom and bride will be heard in you no more". Panel 6 (Revelation 19:7-9): the risen Jesus in light beside the Bride in white, with three guests in white robes. Caption: "Her end: a wedding." The angel says: "Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb." Panel 7 (Revelation 18:4): a man and a woman walking out of the city street, away from it. Caption: "A voice from heaven." A voice from heaven says: "Come out of her, my people, lest you take part in her sins". Panel 8 (Revelation 22:17): the Bride beside a spring, arm held out to a man walking toward her. Caption: "The Bride calls." The Bride says: "Come." John says: "let the one who desires take the water of life without price". The point: Two women call, and Scripture has already written how each one ends. Come out of Babylon, and answer the Bride’s “Come” (Revelation 18:4; 22:17).
svg.text: Two women, two invitations, two ends
Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι, “Come, I will show you”: the same words for both women
Two women call, and Scripture has already written how each one ends. Come
out of Babylon, and answer the Bride’s “Come” (Revelation 18:4; 22:17).
Both women are John’s pictures: the harlot a city (Revelation 17:18), the Bride God’s people. The beast she sits on is not drawn.
